::: {.key-question}
How do Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in the NEPHU catchment experience emotional wellbeing?
:::

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, the significant challenges Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people face in accessing mental health support was discussed, especially finding and accessing services that are affordable and culturally appropriate.

- An increase in mental health conditions and help seeking in young males was also anecdotally noted and discussed.

- The impact of mental health issues and sorry business on the broader community was also discussed, and flow on effects for community wellbeing.

- Other barriers to accessing mental health services that were discussed included drug/substance use and stigma, limits to the number of sessions accessible under funding arrangements, and over-subscribed mental health services that are unable to cope with demand.

## Cultural Strengths and Emotional Wellbeing

### Positive Wellbeing

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Positive wellbeing score
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
wellbeing_positive <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Resilience_PositiveWellbeing_Score.csv")

# Data wrangling
wellbeing_positive <- wellbeing_positive %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(high_75_100_n:low_0_25_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(high_n   = high_75_100_n,
                medium_n = medium_26_74_n,
                low_n    = low_0_25_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(high_n:low_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("high"),
                starts_with("medium"),
                starts_with("low"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "high"     = "High",
                                              "medium"   = "Medium",
                                              "low"      = "Low",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("High",
                                           "Medium",
                                           "Low",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 30% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne had a high level of positive wellbeing in the four weeks prior to the survey. This equates to approximately 7,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to have a low level of positive wellbeing than males (12% vs. 5.1%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Positive wellbeing was assessed using four questions about the respondent's experience of positive emotional states during the previous four weeks.

The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey. The responses to these questions were combined and scaled to produce an overall score between 0 and 100. Overall scores were classified as Low (0 to 25), Medium (26 to 74), or High (75 to 100) positive wellbeing.

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel calm and peaceful?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often have you been a happy person?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel full of life?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you have a lot of energy?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Kessler 5 Psychological Distress Score

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kessler 5 score
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
wellbeing_kessler <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Resilience_Kessler_Score.csv")

# Data wrangling
wellbeing_kessler <- wellbeing_kessler %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(low_moderate_5_11_n:high_very_high_12_25_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(low_n  = low_moderate_5_11_n,
                high_n = high_very_high_12_25_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(low_n:high_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("high"),
                starts_with("low"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "high"     = "High distress",
                                              "low"      = "Low distress",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("High distress",
                                           "Low distress",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 39% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne had a very high or high level of psychological distress (Kessler 5 Score) in the four weeks prior to the survey. This equates to approximately 10,000 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to have a very high or high level of psychological distress than males (42% vs. 37%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Psychological distress was assessed using the Kessler 5 Score, a measure of non-specific recent psychological distress.

The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey. The responses to these questions were combined and scaled to produce an overall score between 5 and 25. Overall scores were classified as Low/Moderate (5 to 11) or High/Very High (12 to 25) psychological distress.

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel nervous?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel without hope?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel restless or jumpy?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel that everything was an effort?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 4 weeks, about how often did you feel so sad that nothing could cheer you up?
  - All of the time
  - Most of the time
  - Some of the time
  - A little of the time
  - None of the time
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Pearlin Mastery Score

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pearlin score
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
wellbeing_pearlin <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Resilience_Pearlin_Score.csv")

# Data wrangling
wellbeing_pearlin <- wellbeing_pearlin %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(high_level_of_mastery_20_28_n:low_level_of_mastery_7_19_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(low_n  = low_level_of_mastery_7_19_n,
                high_n = high_level_of_mastery_20_28_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(high_n:low_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("high"),
                starts_with("low"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "high"     = "High level of control",
                                              "low"      = "Low level of control",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("High level of control",
                                           "Low level of control",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 66% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne felt that they had a high level of control over their life events and outcomes (Pearlin Mastery Score). This equates to approximately 15,400 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely to report a high level of control over their life events and outcomes than females (77% vs. 52%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The level of perceived level of control over life events and outcomes was assessed using the Pearlin Mastery Scale, consisting of seven statements about a person's belief in their ability to control their own life.

All people aged 15 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey were asked how well each of the following statements applied to them. The responses to these statements were combined and scaled to produce an overall score between 7 and 28. Overall scores were classified as a Low (7 to 19) or High (20 to 28) level of control over life events and outcomes.

- There is really no way I can solve some of the problems I have.
  - Strongly agree
  - Agree
  - Disagree
  - Strongly disagree
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Sometimes I feel that I'm being pushed around in life.

  - Agree
  - Disagree
  - Strongly disagree
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- I have little control over the things that happen to me.

  - Strongly disagree
  - Don't know

- I often feel helpless in deaing with the problems of life.
  - Strongly agree
  - Agree
  - Disagree
  - Strongly disagree
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- What happens to me in the future mostly depends on me.
  - Strongly agree
  - Agree
  - Disagree
  - Strongly disagree
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- There is little I can do to change many of the important things in my life.
  - Strongly agree
  - Agree
  - Disagree
  - Strongly disagree
  - Don't know
  - Prefer not to answer

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MSPSS score
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
wellbeing_mspss <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Resilience_MSPSS_Score.csv")

# Data wrangling
wellbeing_mspss <- wellbeing_mspss %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(low_support_1_2_9_n:high_support_5_1_7_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(low_n      = low_support_1_2_9_n,
                moderate_n = moderate_support_3_5_n,
                high_n     = high_support_5_1_7_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(low_n:high_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("high"),
                starts_with("moderate"),
                starts_with("low"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "high"     = "High social support",
                                              "moderate" = "Medium social support",
                                              "low"      = "Low social support",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("High social support",
                                           "Medium social support",
                                           "Low social support",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 64% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne felt that they had a high level of social support from their friends and family (Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support Score). This equates to approximately 15,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to report a high level of social support than males (75% vs. 56%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The level of perceived social support was assessed using the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS), consisting of six statements about a person's social support from their friends and family.

All people aged 15 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey were asked how well each of the following statements applied to them. The responses to these statements were combined and scaled to produce an overall score between 1.0 and 7.0. Overall scores were classified as a Low (1.0 to 2.9), Moderate (3.0 to 5.0), or High (5.1 to 7.0) level of social support.

```{r}
#
figure_count <- figure_count + 1

factor_levels <- stringr::str_wrap(levels(wellbeing_mspss$answer), width = 15)

figure_number <- wellbeing_mspss %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & answer != "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 15), levels = factor_levels)) %>%
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = n,
                    y_breaks   = 1000,
                    y_expand   = 1000)

figure_percent <- wellbeing_mspss %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & answer != "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(stringr::str_wrap(answer, width = 15), levels = factor_levels)) %>%
  #
  f_bar_grouped_sex(x_variable = answer,
                    y_variable = prop,
                    y_max      = 100,
                    y_breaks   = 10,
                    y_expand   = 2.5)

f_bar_grouped_combine(figure_number, figure_percent, legend_offset = -0.1)
```

## Self-Reported Mental Health Conditions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mental health conditions, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
mental_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Health_Mental_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "mental") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(mental != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
mental_lga <- mental_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(mental = dplyr::case_when(
    mental == "Has a mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = mental,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mental health conditions, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
mental_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Health_Mental_AgeSex.csv",
                                      variable = "mental") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(mental != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
mental_agesex <- mental_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(mental = dplyr::case_when(
    mental == "Has a mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>%  
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = mental,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 19% (n = 2,156) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition. This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (8.9%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition ranged from 364 (Whittlesea LGA) to 41 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition and the number expected if the rate was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Whittlesea and Hume LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition ranged from 25% (Yarra LGA) to 13% (Nillumbik LGA).

- The number of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition peaked for people aged 20-29 years, then decreased with increasing age for both genders.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

- Has the person been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Arthritis
  - Asthma
  - Cancer (including remission)
  - Dementia (including Alzheimer's)
  - Diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)
  - Heart disease (including heart attack or angina)
  - Kidney disease
  - Lung condition (including COPD or emphysema)
  - Mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
  - Stroke
  - Any other long-term health condition(s)
  - No long-term health condition

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Type of Mental Health Condition

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type of mental health condition
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
mental_type <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Mental_Type.csv")

# Data wrangling
mental_type <- mental_type %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = total_n - not_applicable_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(substance_n   = harmful_use_or_dependence_on_alcohol_or_drugs_n,
                behavioural_n = behavioural_or_emotional_problems_n,
                other_n       = other_mental_health_condition_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(depression_n:other_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("anxiety"),
                starts_with("depression"),
                starts_with("behavioural"),
                starts_with("substance"),
                starts_with("other"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "anxiety"     = "Anxiety",
                                              "depression"  = "Depression",
                                              "behavioural" = "Behvioural or emotional",
                                              "substance"   = "Alcohol or substance use",
                                              "other"       = "Other conditions",
                                              "answered"    = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Anxiety",
                                           "Depression",
                                           "Behvioural or emotional",
                                           "Alcohol or substance use",
                                           "Other conditions",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 43% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had been diagnosed with a mental health condition at any point during their life. This equates to approximately 16,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely than females to have ever been diagnosed with a mental health condition (45% vs. 41%).

- The most commonly reported mental health conditions by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne were anxiety (84% of survey respondents who had ever been diagnosed with a mental health condition, approximately 14,000 people) and depression (62% of survey respondents who had ever been diagnosed with a mental health condition, approximately 10,300 people).

- For people who had ever been diagnosed with a mental health condition, females were more likely to report anxiety (93% vs. 77%) or depression (73% vs. 53%), and males were more likely to report harmful use or dependence on alcohol or other drugs (30% vs. 10%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Have you ever been told by a doctor, nurse, or other health professional that you have any of these conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Depression
  - Anxiety
  - Harmful use or dependence on alcohol or drugs
  - Behavioural or emotional problems
  - Other mental health condition (please specify)
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- *Anxiety* includes feeling anxious, nervous, or tense; panic disorders; panic attack; phobic anxiety disorders; obsessive compulsive disorder; post traumatic stress disorder; and other anxiety related disorders.

- *Depression* includes feeling depressed and postnatal depression.

- *Behavioural or emotional problems* includes attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD); conduct disorders in children, adolescents, and adults; other behavioural and emotional problems with usual onset in childhood or adolescence; personality disorders (all forms); and habit and impulse disorders.

- *Other conditions* includes organic mental disorders; other mood (affective) disorders; problems of psychological development; schizophrenia; psychosis; and other mental and behavioural problems.
:::

## Use of Mental Health Services

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mental health services - lifetime
# Data from ABS Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
mental_status <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Mental_Status.csv")

# Data wrangling
mental_status <- mental_status %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(has_accessed_used_health_services_for_mental_health_condition_n:has_never_accessed_used_health_services_for_mental_health_condition_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(service_n   = has_accessed_used_health_services_for_mental_health_condition_n,
                noservice_n = has_never_accessed_used_health_services_for_mental_health_condition_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(service_n:noservice_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("service"),
                starts_with("noservice"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "service"   = "Yes",
                                              "noservice" = "No",
                                              "answered"  = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mental health services - type of services used in previous 12 months
# Data from ABS Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
mental_service <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Mental_Service.csv")

# Data wrangling
mental_service <- mental_service %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(other_n    = mental_health_nurse_n + traditional_healer_n + other_n,
                answered_n = total_n - not_applicable_n - did_not_access_services_for_own_mental_health_in_the_last_12_months_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(counselling_n = counselling_service_n,
                gp_n          = general_practitioner_for_mental_health_n,
                ams_n         = aboriginal_medical_service_community_clinic_n,
                psych_n       = psychiatrist_psychologist_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(counselling_n:other_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("counselling"),
                starts_with("gp"),
                starts_with("ams"),
                starts_with("psych"),
                starts_with("other"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "counselling" = "Counselling service",
                                              "gp"          = "General practitioner",
                                              "ams"         = "AMS or Community Clinic",
                                              "psych"       = "Psychiatrist or psychologist",
                                              "other"       = "Other services",
                                              "answered"    = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Counselling service",
                                           "General practitioner",
                                           "AMS or Community Clinic",
                                           "Psychiatrist or psychologist",
                                           "Other services",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 57% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had used or accessed a health service for mental health related conditions during their lifetime. This equates to approximately 14,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely than males to have ever used or accessed a health service for mental health related conditions (66% vs. 49%).

- For Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne who had accessed or used health services for their own mental health during the 12 months prior to the survey, the most common services were counselling services (71%, approximately 5,500 people) and general practitioners (56%, approximately 4,300 people).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- Have you ever accessed or used health services for a mental health condition?
  - Yes
  - No
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Have you been to a counselling service for your own health in the last 12 months?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 12 months, have you accessed or used any other health services for your own mental health?
  - Yes
  - No
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If yes, which of these health services did you seek support from for your own mental health? (Select all that apply)
  - General practitioner
  - Aboriginal Medical Service or Community Clinic
  - Psychiatrist or psychologist
  - Mental health nurse
  - Traditional healer
  - Other (please specify)

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Hospital Admissions

### Mental and Behavioural Disorders

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - mental and behavioural disorders
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_mental <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                              column_select = "admissions_for_mental_health_related_conditions_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_mental <- hospital_mental %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 3,970 hospital admissions for mental and behavioural disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for mental and behavioural disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 589 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 55 (Craigieburn/Sunbury IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for mental and behavioural disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 5,712 per 100,000 population (Whitehorse IARE) to 907 per 100,000 population (Craigieburn/Sunbury IARE).

- 7 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for mental and behavioural disorders above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Whitehorse, Melbourne/Port Phillip, Melbourne East, Melbourne North-East, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Moreland/Broadmeadows, and Maroondah IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for mental and behavioural disorders are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - F00-F09: Organic, including symptomatic, mental disorders
  - F10-F19: Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use
  - F20-F29: Schizophrenia, schizotypal, and delusional disorders
  - F30-F39: Mood (affective) disorders
  - F40-F48: Neurotic, stress-related, and somatoform disorders
  - F50-F59: Behavioural syndromes associated with physiological disturbances and physical factors
  - F60-F69: Disorders of adult personality and behaviour
  - F70-F79: Mental retardation
  - F80-F89: Disorders of psychological development
  - F90-F98: Behavioural and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence
  - F99: Mental disorder, not otherwise specified

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

:::: {.panel-tabset}

:::

```{r}
figure_count <- figure_count + 1

figure_number <- hospital_mental %>% 
  f_bar_simple_iare(y_variable = aboriginal_n,
                    y_breaks   = 100,
                    y_expand   = 35,
                    hospital   = "admission")

figure_percent <- hospital_mental %>% 
  f_bar_simple_iare(y_variable = aboriginal_rate,
                    y_breaks   = 1000,
                    y_expand   = 500,
                    hospital   = "admission")

f_bar_simple_combine(figure_number, figure_percent)
```

### Mood (Affective) Disorders

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - mood (affective) disorders
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_mood <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                            column_select = "admissions_for_mood_affective_disorders_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_mood <- hospital_mood %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 803 hospital admissions for mood (affective) disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for mood (affective) disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 101 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 12 (Craigieburn/Sunbury IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for mood (affective) disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 1,928 per 100,000 population (Whitehorse IARE) to 201 per 100,000 population (Craigieburn/Sunbury IARE).

- 5 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for mood (affective) disorders above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Whitehorse, Melbourne East, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Moreland/Broadmeadows, and Melbourne/Port Phillip IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for mood (affective) disorders are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - F30: Manic episode
  - F31: Bipolar affective disorder
  - F32: Depressive episode
  - F33: Recurrent depressive disorder
  - F34: Persistent mood (affective) disorders
  - F38: Other mood (affective) disorders
  - F39: Unspecified mood (affective) disorder

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Emergency Presentations

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Emergency presentations - mental and behavioural disorders
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
emergency_mental <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "ED_total",
                                               column_select = "emergency_department_presentations_total_presentations_for_mental_and_behavioural_disorders_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
emergency_mental <- emergency_mental %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- Between 01 July 2019 and 30 June 2020 there were 1,142 emergency department presentations for mental and behavioural disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of emergency department presentations for mental and behavioural disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 182 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 15 (Maroondah IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of presentations for mental and behavioural disorders for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 7,086 per 100,000 population (Melbourne/Port Phillip IARE) to 1,265 per 100,000 population (Yarra Ranges IARE).

- 6 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised rate of emergency department presentations for mental and behavioural disorders above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Melbourne/Port Phillip, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Melbourne East, Moreland/Broadmeadows, Melbourne North-East, and Whitehorse IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Emergency department presentations for mental and behavioural disorders are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - F00-F09: Organic, including symptomatic, mental disorders
  - F10-F19: Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use
  - F20-F29: Schizophrenia, schizotypal, and delusional disorders
  - F30-F39: Mood (affective) disorders
  - F40-F48: Neurotic, stress-related, and somatoform disorders
  - F50-F59: Behavioural syndromes associated with physiological disturbances and physical factors
  - F60-F69: Disorders of adult personality and behaviour
  - F70-F79: Mental retardation
  - F80-F89: Disorders of psychological development
  - F90-F98: Behavioural and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence
  - F99: Mental disorder, not otherwise specified

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
